subject: general
question: The Parliament of India can legislate on a state subject if ________ .

options.text: Council of state passes a resolut by 2/3 majority of present
Lok Sabha passes a resolution by simple majority
Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by simple majority

solution:
The correct answer is __**Council of State passes a resolution by 2/3 majority of present.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Article 249** of the **Indian Constitution** provides the Parliament the authority to legislate on matters enumerated in the State List if the **Rajya Sabha passes a resolution** by a **two-thirds majority of the members present and voting**.
 
• Such a resolution must declare that the subject is of **national importance** and necessary for Parliament to enact laws on the matter.
 
• Once the resolution is passed, Parliament can legislate on the state subject for a period of **one year**. This period can be extended by passing another resolution.
